liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **To Lay Me Down** (3 reviews): Called a lovely, lyrical rendition; Called a great version within the acoustic set [6][8][9]
- **Rosalie McFall** (2 reviews): Part of a three-song run with I Hear a Voice Calling and Swing Low, showing a simple folksy Dead; Praised along with To Lay Me Down [6][7]
- **Swing Low, Sweet Chariot** (1 review): Reviewer finds it interesting to hear the Dead play this song [7]

## Setlist highlights

- **A Voice From On High**: rare: 5 archived performances [15]
- **Swing Low, Sweet Chariot**: rare: 13 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd70-07-30.sbd.cotsman.17077.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 6 songs; 33 min; rated 3.67/5 by 12 [1]. Said about its sound: Labeled soundboard and clear, but with some noticeable sound issues; Some sound problems; banter and gaps between songs add little; vocals and guitar are good; Slightly muddy because the bass is too loud [3][7][9][12][13]
- **gd1970-07-30.sbd.boswell.smith.114020.flac16**: soundboard; 6 songs; 33 min; rated 1/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: This Boswell/Smith transfer has high hiss from many generations of transfer [10]

## Around the show

- Short set capturing the Dead deep in their folksy acoustic phase of 1970 [6]
- Only the acoustic set survives, which the reviewer considers the most important part of a 1970 show [8]
- Represents the gospel-leaning Grateful Dead at their best [10]
- Reviewer describes the set as relaxed country and gospel music, suited to drinking beer with friends [11]
- Reviewer wishes the set were longer [13]
- John Dawson and David Nelson joined on I Hear A Voice Callin and Swing Low Sweet Chariot [1]
- Acoustic first set listed under NRPS, with John Dawson and David Nelson joining [2]
- A solid set, but better acoustic Dead sets exist [3]
- The Cotsman remaster handles noise and clutter better than this version [10]
- Sound is acceptable compared with other acoustic shows from this period [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-07-30.sbd.cotsman.17077.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Chuck Gannon and JCotsman; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Sound Forge was used for slight pitch correction and minor edits [1]
- **gd1970-07-30.sbd.boswell.smith.114020.flac16**: taped by Will Boswell; transferred by Matt Smith; source: MR(Abrams)>R@ 7.5 ips.(Peter Kafer)>R @ 7.5 ips.(Will Boswell) > CD; Transfered and mastered by Matt Smith 5/11; cd > flac dbpoweramp cd ripper [2]. Also: CD ripped with dbpoweramp to FLAC, with checksums, by gballen in June 2011 [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Crimson Records: [GRATEFUL DEAD - The Matrix '70 - Crimson Records](https://crimsonrecords.com.ar/product/grateful-dead-the-matrix-70/) [16]
